requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.fingerprints`. The cited requirements are context only, so I did not reassess them.

**SHA-256 over words**
- `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` in `tests/outline_content.rs` checks that the Rust case gives a 64-character hex digest.
- The same test checks that whitespace-only edits keep the hash and that `two words` differs from `twowords`.
- `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` and `string_literals_hash_as_words` in `src/outline/tests.rs` cover the same word-boundary rule for doc prose and string literals.
- The tests do not compare against a known SHA-256 vector. I treat the 64-hex check as sufficient and do not count it as a gap.

**Fingerprint scheme**
- `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` asserts `language.fingerprint_scheme()` equals `"rust-structural-v1"`.
- It also asserts that `OutlineContent::fingerprint_scheme()` retains the language's scheme.

**Doc comments participate**
- `editing_a_doc_comment_word_changes_the_hash` and `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` assert that changing a doc word (`Doc.` to `Docs.`, `total` for `count`) changes the hash.
- `reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` asserts that changing words or their order changes the hash.

**Ordinary comments excluded**
- The `// {cite}` line comment in `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` is changed from `a.b` to `c.d`, and the hash is unchanged.
- The `/* note */` to `/* edited */` change in the Rust case of the bundled fingerprint test also leaves the hash unchanged.

**Delimiters excluded, reflowing, consecutive comments as one sequence**
- `reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` shows `/// a` followed by `/// b` equals `/// a b`, `/** a * b */`, and the padded or blank-line variant with extra spaces.
- `reflowing_inner_and_block_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` shows `//!` lines equal `/*! */`, and a `/** * */` block with leading `*` equals `///`.
- `editing_a_doc_comment_word_changes_the_hash` confirms that splitting words across lines keeps the hash.
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` confirms the same for a reformatted item.

**Inner and outer groups**
- `inner_and_outer_doc_comments_hash_in_separate_groups` asserts that moving `two` from a nested item's outer doc into the module's inner doc changes the module hash.
- It also asserts that splitting words across consecutive inner comments keeps the hash.
- The inner-versus-outer case moves the text between an inner comment on the module and an outer comment on a nested item, so the attachment structure differs as well as the group. The test therefore does not fully isolate group tagging. I judged it adequate because it exercises the "moving text between groups changes the hash" scenario and the implementation (`doc_prose` in `languages/rust.rs`) returns a distinct group per comment.

**Attributes participate**
- `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` asserts that changing `#[inline]` to `#[cold]` changes the hash.
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` checks the item span and fingerprint together with the attached attribute and doc comment.
- A body edit (`= 1` to `= 2`) changes the hash, while the node's identity hash stays the same when a descendant changes.

All the tests are marked with `{test}` references to this requirement. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
